sanskrit: sa sāgaram anādhṛṣyam atikramya mahābalaḥ trikūṭaśikhare laṅkāṃ sthitāṃ svastho dadarśa ha
english: Having crossed the irresistible ocean, that mighty one beheld Laṅkā standing on the peak of Trikūṭa, and stood at ease.

sanskrit: tataḥ pādapamuktena puṣpavarṣeṇa vīryavān abhivṛṣṭaḥ sthitas tatra babhau puṣpamayo yathā
english: Then, as he stood there, the valiant one was showered by a rain of flowers shed from the trees, and shone as though made of blossoms.

sanskrit: yojanānāṃ śataṃ śrīmāṃs tīrtvāpy uttamavikramaḥ aniśvasan kapis tatra na glānim adhigacchati
english: Though the glorious ape of supreme prowess had crossed a hundred yojanas, he did not breathe hard and felt no fatigue there.

sanskrit: śatāny ahaṃ yojanānāṃ krameyaṃ subahūny api kiṃ punaḥ sāgarasyāntaṃ saṃkhyātaṃ śatayojanam
english: "I could stride many hundreds of yojanas — how much less this ocean whose end is measured at a hundred yojanas!"

sanskrit: sa tu vīryavatāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ plavatām api cottamaḥ jagāma vegavāṃl laṅkāṃ laṅghayitvā mahodadhim
english: He who is the best among the mighty and the foremost of leapers, having vaulted the great ocean, swiftly came to Laṅkā.

sanskrit: śādvalāni ca nīlāni gandhavanti vanāni ca gaṇḍavanti ca madhyena jagāma nagavanti ca
english: He passed through dark-green meadows, fragrant forests, groves with prominent peaks, and mountain-bearing tracts.

sanskrit: śailāṃś ca tarusaṃchannān vanarājīś ca puṣpitāḥ abhicakrāma tejasvī hanumān plavagarṣabhaḥ
english: The lustrous Hanūmān, the bull among leapers, passed over hills covered with trees and flowering forest-rows.

sanskrit: sa tasminn acale tiṣṭhan vanāny upavanāni ca sa nagāgre ca tāṃ laṅkāṃ dadarśa pavanātmajaḥ
english: Standing on that mountain, the son of the wind god beheld forests and groves; and from the mountain's peak he saw Laṅkā.

sanskrit: saralān karṇikārāṃś ca kharjūrāṃś ca supuṣpitān priyālān muculindāṃś ca kuṭajān ketakān api
english: He saw sāra pines, karṇikāra trees, date palms in full bloom, priyāla and muculinda trees, kuṭaja shrubs, and ketaka plants.

sanskrit: priyaṅgūn gandhapūrṇāṃś ca nīpān saptacchadāṃs tathā asanān kovidārāṃś ca karavīrāṃś ca puṣpitān
english: He saw priyaṅgu vines full of fragrance, nīpa trees, saptacchadā trees, asana trees, kovidāras, and karavīra shrubs in bloom.

sanskrit: puṣpabhāranibaddhāṃś ca tathā mukulitān api pādapān vihagākīrṇān pavanādhūtamastakān
english: He saw trees weighed down with loads of flowers, some still in bud, covered with birds, their crowns tossed by the wind.

sanskrit: haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇā vāpīḥ padmotpalāyutāḥ ākrīḍān vividhān ramyān vividhāṃś ca jalāśayān
english: He beheld ponds thronged with haṃsa and kāraṇḍava birds, adorned with lotuses and blue water-lilies, many delightful pleasure-groves, and various reservoirs.

sanskrit: saṃtatān vividhair vṛkṣaiḥ sarvartuphalapuṣpitaiḥ udyānāni ca ramyāṇi dadarśa kapikuñjaraḥ
english: The bull among apes saw gardens densely planted with various trees that bore fruit and flowers in every season.

sanskrit: samāsādya ca lakṣmīvāṃl laṅkāṃ rāvaṇapālitām parikhābhiḥ sapadmābhiḥ sotpalābhir alaṃkṛtām
english: Approaching it, the glorious one beheld Laṅkā, guarded by Rāvaṇa, adorned with moats filled with lotuses and blue water-lilies.

sanskrit: sītāpaharaṇārthena rāvaṇena surakṣitām samantād vicaradbhiś ca rākṣasair ugradhanvibhiḥ
english: It was well-guarded by Rāvaṇa on account of his abduction of Sītā, and patrolled on all sides by rākṣasas carrying fierce bows.

sanskrit: kāñcanenāvṛtāṃ ramyāṃ prākāreṇa mahāpurīm aṭṭālakaśatākīrṇāṃ patākādhvajamālinīm
english: The great city was encircled by a golden rampart, beautiful and covered with hundreds of watchtowers, garlanded with banners and standards.

sanskrit: toraṇaiḥ kāñcanair divyair latāpaṅktivicitritaiḥ dadarśa hanumāṃl laṅkāṃ divi devapurīm iva
english: Hanūmān saw Laṅkā with its divine golden gateways embellished with rows of creepers — like a city of the gods in heaven.

sanskrit: girimūrdhni sthitāṃ laṅkāṃ pāṇḍurair bhavanaiḥ śubhaiḥ dadarśa sa kapiḥ śrīmān puram ākāśagaṃ yathā
english: The glorious ape beheld Laṅkā set on the mountain's summit, with white and beautiful mansions — like a city floating in the sky.

sanskrit: pālitāṃ rākṣasendreṇa nirmitāṃ viśvakarmaṇā plavamānām ivākāśe dadarśa hanumān purīm
english: Hanūmān saw the city protected by the lord of rākṣasas, built by Viśvakarman, appearing as though it floated in the sky.

sanskrit: saṃpūrṇāṃ rākṣasair ghorair nāgair bhogavatīm iva acintyāṃ sukṛtāṃ spaṣṭāṃ kuberādhyuṣitāṃ purā
english: Filled with terrible rākṣasas and serpents like Bhogavatī, inconceivable, well-built, splendid — formerly inhabited by Kubera himself.

sanskrit: daṃṣṭribhir bahubhiś cūraiḥ śūlapaṭṭiśapāṇibhiḥ rakṣitāṃ rākṣasair ghorair guhām āśīviṣair api
english: It was guarded by many fanged warriors, terrible rākṣasas holding spears and battle-axes in their hands, like a cave of venomous serpents.

sanskrit: vapraprākārajaghanāṃ vipulāmbunavāmbarām śataghnīśūlakeśāntām aṭṭālakavataṃsakām
english: Its hips were the earthen rampart and walls; its robe was the great mass of water; its locks were tipped with śataghnī engines and spears; its ornament was the row of watchtowers.

sanskrit: dvāram uttaram āsādya cintayām āsa vānaraḥ kailāsaśikharaprakhyam ālikhantam ivāmbaram dhriyamāṃam ivākāśam ucchritair bhavanottamaiḥ
english: Approaching the northern gate, the monkey reflected — it was like the peak of Kailāsa, as if scratching the sky, as if holding the firmament aloft with its towering mansions.

sanskrit: tasyāś ca mahatīṃ guptiṃ sāgaraṃ ca nirīkṣya saḥ rāvaṇaṃ ca ripuṃ ghoraṃ cintayām āsa vānaraḥ
english: Having surveyed its mighty defenses and the ocean, and reflecting upon Rāvaṇa the terrible enemy, the monkey fell into thought.

sanskrit: āgatyāpīha harayo bhaviṣyanti nirarthakāḥ na hi yuddhena vai laṅkā śakyā jetuṃ surair api
english: "Even if the monkeys came here, they would be in vain. Laṅkā cannot be conquered in battle even by the gods."

sanskrit: imāṃ tu viṣamāṃ durgāṃ laṅkāṃ rāvaṇapālitām prāpyāpi sa mahābāhuḥ kiṃ kariṣyati rāghavaḥ
english: "Even having reached this inaccessible fortress, Laṅkā protected by Rāvaṇa — what will the long-armed Rāghava do?"

sanskrit: avakāśo na sāntvasya rākṣaseṣv abhigamyate na dānasya na bhedasya naiva yuddhasya dṛśyate
english: "No scope for conciliation is found among the rākṣasas; no scope for bribery or sowing dissension is visible; nor even for battle."

sanskrit: caturṇām eva hi gatir vānarāṇāṃ mahātmanām vāliputrasya nīlasya mama rājñaś ca dhīmataḥ
english: "The passage belongs only to four of the great-souled monkeys: the son of Vālī, Nīla, myself, and the wise king."

sanskrit: yāvaj jānāmi vaidehīṃ yadi jīvati vā na vā tatraiva cintayiṣyāmi dṛṣṭvā tāṃ janakātmajām
english: "Until I learn of Vaidehī — whether she lives or not — I shall deliberate only after seeing Janaka's daughter."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa cintayām āsa muhūrtaṃ kapikuñjaraḥ giriśṛṅge sthitas tasmin rāmasyābhyudaye rataḥ
english: Then the bull among apes, devoted to Rāma's welfare, stood for a moment on that mountain peak, deep in thought.

sanskrit: anena rūpeṇa mayā na śakyā rakṣasāṃ purī praveṣṭuṃ rākṣasair guptā krūrair balasamanvitaiḥ
english: "In this form, I cannot enter the city of the rākṣasas, guarded as it is by cruel and powerful rākṣasas."

sanskrit: ugraojaso mahāvīryo balavantaś ca rākṣasāḥ vañcanīyā mayā sarve jānakīṃ parimārgitā
english: "All these rākṣasas of fierce energy, great valor, and great strength must be deceived by me in my search for Jānakī."

sanskrit: lakṣyālakṣyeṇa rūpeṇa rātrau laṅkā purī mayā praveṣṭuṃ prāptakālaṃ me kṛtyaṃ sādhayituṃ mahat
english: "In a form barely visible, at night, I should enter the city of Laṅkā — the time is ripe for me to accomplish this great task."

sanskrit: tāṃ purīṃ tādṛśīṃ dṛṣṭvā durādharṣāṃ surāsuraiḥ hanūmāṃś cintayām āsa viniḥśvasya muhur muhuḥ
english: Seeing that city thus — inaccessible to gods and asuras — Hanūmān reflected, sighing again and again.

sanskrit: kenopāyena paśyeyaṃ maithilīṃ janakātmajām adṛṣṭo rākṣasendreṇa rāvaṇena durātmanā
english: "By what means might I see Maithilī, Janaka's daughter, without being seen by Rāvaṇa the evil-souled lord of rākṣasas?"

sanskrit: na vinaśyet kathaṃ kāryaṃ rāmasya viditātmanaḥ ekām ekaś ca paśyeyaṃ rahite janakātmajām
english: "How should the mission of the self-knowing Rāma not be ruined? And how should I, alone, see Janaka's daughter alone and in private?"

sanskrit: bhūtāś cārtho vipadyante deśakālavirodhitāḥ viklavaṃ dūtam āsādya tamaḥ sūryodaye yathā
english: "Accomplished purposes collapse when contrary to place and time, and when they meet with a confused envoy — as darkness collapses at sunrise."

sanskrit: arthānarthāntare buddhir niścitāpi na śobhate ghātayanti hi kāryāṇi dūtāḥ paṇḍitamāninaḥ
english: "Even a settled judgment does not shine at the boundary between advantage and disadvantage; for envoys who fancy themselves wise destroy missions."

sanskrit: na vinaśyet kathaṃ kāryaṃ vaiklavyaṃ na kathaṃ bhavet laṅghanaṃ ca samudrasya kathaṃ nu na vṛthā bhavet
english: "How should the mission not be ruined? How should confusion not arise? And how should my crossing of the ocean not be in vain?"

sanskrit: mayi dṛṣṭe tu rakṣobhī rāmasya viditātmanaḥ bhaved vyartham idaṃ kāryaṃ rāvaṇānartham icchataḥ
english: "If the rākṣasas see me, this mission of the self-knowing Rāma, who wishes ill to Rāvaṇa, would become fruitless."

sanskrit: na hi śakyaṃ kva cit sthātum avijñātena rākṣasaiḥ api rākṣasarūpeṇa kim utānyena kena cit
english: "It is impossible to remain anywhere without being recognized by the rākṣasas — even in rākṣasa form, much less in any other form."

sanskrit: vāyur apy atra nājñātaś cared iti matir mama na hy asty aviditaṃ kiṃ cid rākṣasānāṃ balīyasām
english: "My belief is that not even the wind moves here unrecognized; for there is nothing unknown to these mighty rākṣasas."

sanskrit: ihāhaṃ yadi tiṣṭhāmi svena rūpeṇa saṃvṛtaḥ vināśam upayāsyāmi bhartur arthaś ca hīyate
english: "If I remain here disguised in my own form, I shall meet destruction, and my master's cause will suffer."

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ svena rūpeṇa rajanyāṃ hrasvatāṃ gataḥ laṅkām abhipatiṣyāmi rāghavasyārthasiddhaye
english: "Therefore, having taken a diminutive form from my own nature, I shall fly into Laṅkā by night, for the accomplishment of Rāghava's purpose."

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya purīṃ rātrau praviśya sudurāsadām vicinvan bhavanaṃ sarvaṃ drakṣyāmi janakātmajām
english: "Entering by night this city of Rāvaṇa so difficult to assault, searching every mansion, I shall find Janaka's daughter."

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya hanumān sūryasyāstamayaṃ kapiḥ ācakāṅkṣe tadā vīrā vaidehyā darśanotsukaḥ pṛṣadaṃśakamātraḥ san babhūvādbhutadarśanaḥ
english: Having thus deliberated, the heroic Hanūmān awaited the setting of the sun, eager to see Vaidehī, and having made himself the size of a mere gnat, he became wondrous to behold.

sanskrit: pradoṣakāle hanumāṃs tūrṇam utpatya vīryavān praviveśa purīṃ ramyāṃ suvibhaktamahāpatham
english: At dusk, the valiant Hanūmān swiftly sprang up and entered the beautiful city with its broad, well-laid avenues.

sanskrit: prāsādamālāvitatāṃ stambhaiḥ kāñcanarājataiḥ śātakumbhamayair jālair gandharvanagaropamām
english: It was spread with rows of palaces, with golden and silver pillars, with lattices of pure gold — resembling the city of the gandharvas.

sanskrit: saptabhaumāṣṭabhaumaiś ca sa dadarśa mahāpurīm talaiḥ sphāṭikasaṃpūrṇaiḥ kārtasvaravibhūṣitaiḥ
english: He saw the great city with its seven- and eight-storied buildings, with floors filled with crystal and adorned with pure gold.

sanskrit: vaidūryamaṇicitraiś ca muktājālavibhūṣitaiḥ talaiḥ śuśubhire tāni bhavanāny atra rakṣasām
english: The mansions of the rākṣasas there shone with floors decorated with vaidūrya gems and adorned with nets of pearls.

sanskrit: kāñcanāni vicitrāṇi toraṇāni ca rakṣasām laṅkām uddyotayām āsuḥ sarvataḥ samalaṃkṛtām
english: The golden and variegated gateways of the rākṣasas lit up Laṅkā, which was adorned and embellished on all sides.

sanskrit: acintyām adbhutākārāṃ dṛṣṭvā laṅkāṃ mahākapiḥ āsīd viṣaṇṇo hṛṣṭaś ca vaidehyā darśanotsukaḥ
english: Beholding Laṅkā, inconceivable and of wondrous form, the great monkey was at once downcast and elated, eager to see Vaidehī.

sanskrit: sa pāṇḍurodviddhavimānamālinīṃ mahārhajāmbūnadajālatoraṇām yaśasvināṃ rāvaṇabāhupālitāṃ kṣapācarair bhīmabalaiḥ samāvṛtām
english: He gazed at it — garlanded with white, soaring aerial pavilions, with gateways latticed with precious jāmbūnada gold, protected by the arms of the glorious Rāvaṇa, surrounded by night-roaming beings of terrible power.

sanskrit: candro 'pi sācivyam ivāsya kurvaṃs tārāgaṇair madhyagato virājan jyotsnāvitānena vitatya lokam uttiṣṭhate naikasahasraraśmiḥ
english: And the moon, as though rendering service to Laṅkā, rising resplendent surrounded by hosts of stars, spreading a canopy of moonlight over the world, rose with its thousands upon thousands of rays.

sanskrit: śaṅkhaprabhaṃ kṣīramṛṇālavarṇam udgacchamānaṃ vyavabhāsamānam dadarśa candraṃ sa kapipravīraḥ poplūyamānaṃ sarasīva haṃsaṃ
english: That foremost of monkeys saw the moon rising and shining — bright as a conch, white as milk and lotus-fiber — gliding like a haṃsa upon a lake.

sanskrit: sa lambaśikhare lambe lambatoyadasaṃnibhe sattvam āsthāya medhāvī hanumān mārutātmajaḥ
english: On a lofty peak, high and resembling a hanging cloud, the wise Hanūmān, son of the wind, composed himself with courage.

sanskrit: niśi laṅkāṃ mahāsattvo viveśa kapikuñjaraḥ ramyakānanatoyāḍhyāṃ purīṃ rāvaṇapālitām
english: At night, Hanūmān the great-souled bull among apes entered Laṅkā — the city protected by Rāvaṇa, rich with beautiful groves and waters.

sanskrit: śāradāmbudharaprakhyair bhavanair upaśobhitām sāgaropamanirghoṣāṃ sāgarānilasevitām
english: It was beautified by mansions resembling autumnal clouds; its roar was like the ocean; it was fanned by the ocean wind.

sanskrit: supuṣṭabalasaṃguptāṃ yathaiva viṭapāvatīm cārutoraṇaniryūhāṃ pāṇḍuradvāratoraṇām
english: Guarded by a well-nourished army — like Viṭapāvatī herself — with beautiful gateway-arches and white-pillared portals.

sanskrit: bhujagācaritāṃ guptāṃ śubhāṃ bhogavatīm iva tāṃ savidyudghanākīrṇāṃ jyotirmārganiṣevitām
english: Frequented by serpentine beings and well-guarded, beautiful — like Bhogavatī — covered with clouds shot through with lightning, and traversed by pathways of luminaries.

sanskrit: caṇḍamārutanirhrādāṃ yathendrasyāmarāvatīm śātakumbhena mahatā prākāreṇābhisaṃvṛtām
english: Resounding with fierce winds like Indra's Amarāvatī, surrounded by a great rampart of pure gold.

sanskrit: kiṅkiṇījālaghoṣābhiḥ patākābhir alaṃkṛtām āsādya sahasā hṛṣṭaḥ prākāram abhipedivān
english: Adorned with banners ringing with clusters of tiny bells, he approached suddenly, joyful, and reached the rampart.

sanskrit: vismayāviṣṭahṛdayaḥ purīm ālokya sarvataḥ jāmbūnadamayair dvārair vaidūryakṛtavedikaiḥ
english: His heart seized with wonder, surveying the city on all sides — with gateways made of jāmbūnada gold and raised platforms fashioned of vaidūrya gems —

sanskrit: maṇisphaṭikamuktābhir maṇikuṭṭimabhūṣitaiḥ taptahāṭakaniryūhai rājatāmalapāṇḍuraiḥ
english: — adorned with gem-inlaid floors of sapphire, crystal, and pearl; with projecting cornices of refined gold; gleaming silver-white and spotless —

sanskrit: vaidūryatalasopānaiḥ sphāṭikāntarapāṃsubhiḥ cārusaṃjavanopetaiḥ kham ivotpatitaiḥ śubhaiḥ
english: — with staircases of vaidūrya, with crystal dust between the steps, fitted with beautiful running-courses, those auspicious mansions seemed to soar into the sky —

sanskrit: krauñcabarhiṇasaṃghuṣṭe rājahaṃsaniṣevitaiḥ tūryābharaṇanirghoṣaiḥ sarvataḥ pratināditām
english: — resounding everywhere with the cries of krauñca birds and peacocks, frequented by royal haṃsas, reverberating with the sounds of musical instruments and ornaments —

sanskrit: vasvokasārāpratimāṃ samīkṣya nagarīṃ tataḥ kham ivotpatitāṃ laṅkāṃ jaharṣa hanumān kapiḥ
english: Surveying that city matchless as Vasvokasārā, Laṅkā appearing to leap into the sky, the monkey Hanūmān rejoiced.

sanskrit: tāṃ samīkṣya purīṃ laṅkāṃ rākṣasādhipateḥ śubhām anuttamām ṛddhiyutāṃ cintayām āsa vīryavān
english: Surveying that city Laṅkā of the lord of rākṣasas — beautiful, unrivaled, full of prosperity — the valiant one fell into thought.

sanskrit: neyam anyena nagarī śakyā dharṣayituṃ balāt rakṣitā rāvaṇabalair udyatāyudhadhāribhiḥ
english: "This city cannot be assaulted by force by anyone else, guarded as it is by the armies of Rāvaṇa with weapons raised and ready."

sanskrit: kumudāṅgadayor vāpi suṣeṇasya mahākapeḥ prasiddheyaṃ bhaved bhūmir maindadvividayor api
english: "This ground might be within the reach of Kumuda and Aṅgada, of the great monkey Suṣeṇa, and also of Mainda and Dvivida."

sanskrit: vivasvatas tanūjasya hareś ca kuśaparvaṇaḥ ṛkṣasya ketumālasya mama caiva gatir bhavet
english: "It might be within reach of Vivasvat's son, of the monkey Kuśaparvan, of Ṛkṣa and Ketumāla, and of myself as well."

sanskrit: samīkṣya tu mahābāho rāghavasya parākramam lakṣmaṇasya ca vikrāntam abhavat prītimān kapiḥ
english: Yet reflecting on the valor of the long-armed Rāghava and on Lakṣmaṇa's prowess, the monkey became confident and glad.

sanskrit: tāṃ ratnavasanopetāṃ koṣṭhāgārāvataṃsakām yantrāgārāstanīm ṛddhāṃ pramadām iva bhūṣitām
english: He saw the city adorned with jewels and garments, crowned with treasure-houses, her breast the arsenal — wealthy, like a great lady adorned with ornaments.

sanskrit: tāṃ naṣṭatimirāṃ dīpair bhāsvaraiś ca mahāgṛhaiḥ nagarīṃ rākṣasendrasya dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ
english: The great monkey saw the city of the lord of rākṣasas — its darkness dispelled by lamps and the luminous great mansions.

sanskrit: praviṣṭaḥ sattvasaṃpanno niśāyāṃ mārutātmajaḥ sa mahāpatham āsthāya muktāpuṣpavirājitam
english: Having entered by night, the son of the wind, full of courage, took the great road adorned and shining with scattered flowers.

sanskrit: hasitodghuṣṭaninadais tūryaghoṣapuraḥsaraiḥ vajrāṅkuśanikāśaiś ca vajrajālavibhūṣitaiḥ gṛhamedhaiḥ purī ramyā babhāse dyaur ivāmbudaiḥ
english: With sounds of laughter and uproar attended by music, with householders' dwellings resembling thunderbolts and hooks, adorned with lattices of lightning — the beautiful city shone like the sky with storm-clouds.

sanskrit: prajajvāla tadā laṅkā rakṣogaṇagṛhaiḥ śubhaiḥ sitābhrasadṛśaiś citraiḥ padmasvastikasaṃsthitaiḥ vardhamānagṛhaiś cāpi sarvataḥ suvibhāṣitaiḥ
english: Laṅkā blazed then with the beautiful homes of the rākṣasa hosts — white as clouds, adorned with lotus and svastika patterns, and with expanding mansions eloquently fashioned on all sides.

sanskrit: tāṃ citramālyābharaṇāṃ kapirājahitaṃkaraḥ rāghavārthaṃ carañ śrīmān dadarśa ca nananda ca
english: Roaming for Rāghava's sake, the glorious one who works for the welfare of the monkey-king saw that city adorned with varied garlands and ornaments, and was delighted.

sanskrit: śuśrāva madhuraṃ gītaṃ tristhānasvarabhūṣitam strīṇāṃ madasamṛddhānāṃ divi cāpsarasām iva
english: He heard sweet song adorned with tones from the three registers — from women intoxicated with wine, like the apsarases in heaven.

sanskrit: śuśrāva kāñcīninādaṃ nūpurāṇāṃ ca niḥsvanam sopānaninadāṃś caiva bhavaneṣu mahātmanam āsphoṭitaninādāṃś ca kṣveḍitāṃś ca tatas tataḥ
english: He heard the tinkling of girdles and the ringing of anklets, the sound of footsteps on staircases in the mansions, and here and there the sounds of clapping and hissing.

sanskrit: svādhyāyaniratāṃś caiva yātudhānān dadarśa saḥ rāvaṇastavasaṃyuktān garjato rākṣasān api
english: He saw yātudhānas engaged in recitation of the Vedas, and rākṣasas roaring praises to Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: rājamārgaṃ samāvṛtya sthitaṃ rakṣobalaṃ mahat dadarśa madhyame gulme rākṣasasya carān bahūn
english: He saw a great body of rākṣasa troops blocking the royal road, and in the central guard-post many scouts of the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: dīkṣitāñ jaṭilān muṇḍān go'jināmbaravāsasaḥ darbhamuṣṭipraharaṇān agnikuṇḍāyudhāṃs tathā
english: He saw some who had taken vows, some matted-haired, some shaven — clothed in cowhides and goatskins, armed with fistfuls of kuśa grass, and others with fire-pots as weapons.

sanskrit: kūṭamudgarapāṇīṃś ca daṇḍāyudhadharān api ekākṣānekakarṇāṃś ca calallambapayodharān
english: He saw those holding crooked clubs, those bearing staff-weapons, one-eyed ones, many-eared ones, and those with swinging, pendulous breasts.

sanskrit: karālān bhugnavaktrāṃś ca vikaṭān vāmanāṃs tathā dhanvinaḥ khaḍginaś caiva śataghnīmusalāyudhān parighottamahastāṃś ca vicitrakavacojjvalān
english: He saw terrible ones, disfigured ones, monstrous and dwarfish ones, archers, swordsmen, those armed with śataghnī engines and clubs, those holding great iron bars in their hands — all gleaming in varied armor.

sanskrit: nātiṣṭhūlān nātikṛśān nātidīrghātihrasvakān virūpān bahurūpāṃś ca surūpāṃś ca suvarcasaḥ
english: He saw those who were neither too stout nor too lean, neither too tall nor too short — some ill-shaped, some of many forms, and some of handsome form and bright complexion.

sanskrit: śaktivṛkṣāyudhāṃś caiva paṭṭiśāśanidhāriṇaḥ kṣepaṇīpāśahastāṃś ca dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ
english: The great monkey also saw those armed with śakti-spears and tree-trunks, those bearing battle-axes and thunderbolts, and those holding slings and nooses in their hands.

sanskrit: sragviṇas tv anuliptāṃś ca varābharaṇabhūṣitān tīkṣṇaśūladharāṃś caiva vajriṇaś ca mahābalān
english: He saw those wearing garlands and anointed with unguents, adorned with excellent ornaments, those bearing sharp tridents, and those carrying the vajra — all of great power.

sanskrit: śatasāhasram avyagram ārakṣaṃ madhyamaṃ kapiḥ prākārāvṛtam atyantaṃ dadarśa sa mahākapiḥ
english: The great monkey saw the central guard of one hundred thousand, unwavering, completely surrounding the rampart.

sanskrit: triviṣṭapanibhaṃ divyaṃ divyanādavināditam vājiheṣitasaṃghuṣṭaṃ nāditaṃ bhūṣaṇais tathā
english: It was like the divine Triviṣṭapa, filled with divine sounds, resounding with the neighing of horses, reverberating with the music of ornaments.

sanskrit: rathair yānair vimānaiś ca tathā gajahayaiḥ śubhaiḥ vāraṇaiś ca caturdantaiḥ śvetābhranicayopamaiḥ
english: There were chariots, vehicles, aerial cars, auspicious elephants and horses, and four-tusked elephants resembling masses of white cloud.

sanskrit: bhūṣitaṃ ruciradvāraṃ mattaiś ca mṛgapakṣibhiḥ rākṣasādhipater guptam āviveśa gṛhaṃ kapiḥ
english: Adorned and with a beautiful gateway, with intoxicated animals and birds — guarded as the mansion of the lord of rākṣasas — the monkey entered.
